title: Personnel on the New Orleans Kings records
summary: Allen and Wiggs name members of the band across two sessions: Emil Christian, Raymond Burke, Paul Barbarin, Jeff Riddick and others.

bands.name: Johnny Wiggs and His New Orleans Kings

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I wanted to mention some of the members of the band and Oscar, yeah, okay, thanks, Oscar. Santa Pecora, Lester Bouchon, Raymond Burke. No?
Okay. What happened is there's two recording sessions put out on the same LP. So you've got two bands there, and you had Emil Christian on the trombone, Raymond Burke.

Yeah. Emil used to be with the original Dixieland Jazz Band. He was a cornet player before he joined the original Dixieland Jazz Band, and it seems like overnight they made him into a trombone player, the story goes. Johnny remembers more about that than I do. But we had Raymond Burke on clarinet there, one of the... The greatest. Yes. Inventive, creative, always has to play something new. Lovely. Anything you want. And, of course, Paul Barberin on drums. Yeah. Sherwood Man Japan on bass. And who's the piano player? Jeff? Jeff Riddick. Jeff Riddick.
That's what I thought. With that beautiful wide tone. How can anybody get a wide tone on piano? Jeff does.

Well, it's just that touch he has. Hmm. And his brother, too. He's from a musical family. His brother, Johnny, played piano with the original Crescent City Jazzers, which was out of Mobile. I never did know why they called themselves the original Crescent City Jazzers. Everybody wants to cash in on the Crescent City, maybe. Well, you find that all over the world. Whether you go to Japan or England or Germany, they'll have something that reminds you of New Orleans.
